title: Proteomic aging clocks go to trial - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A commentary on the first clinical-trial deployment of six proteomic aging clocks. Its stance is that the deployment reveals more about the clocks than about the drug.

themes.theme: Proteomic aging clocks in clinical trials

insights.claim: Six proteomic aging clocks have been deployed together in a clinical trial for the first time.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Marks aging biomarkers moving from observational use to trial endpoints, relevant to longevity-drug development.
insights.quote: Six proteomic aging clocks are deployed in a clinical trial for the first time

insights.claim: The commentary argues the trial results reveal more about the aging clocks' behavior and validity than about the efficacy of the drug tested.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Caution against reading clock movements as proof of drug benefit; clocks need validation as surrogate endpoints before they de-risk longevity programs.
insights.quote: revealing more about the clocks than about the drug
